column1: # Pages the deploy leg (scripts/wp_deploy_on_merge.py) publishes to PRODUCTION when
# `main` advances and their source changed. One slug per line; the slug must be a row
# in wp/pages.tsv.
# Listing a row here is the decision that a merge to main IS its release. Rows that
# must stay a deliberate hand step do not belong here:
#   * guide-download-staging — 4587 is a staging draft whose slug 404s.
#   * guide-waitlist-confirmed — NOT a draft: 4809 was published September 19, 2026
#     (see wp/pages.tsv and docs/guide-release-runbook.md). It is held off this list
#     as a hand step; whether it should be added is an open decision, not a fact about
#     its status.
#   * how-to-select-a-tms, tms-selection-mistakes — those rows carry STAGING post ids;
#     writing them to production would overwrite a different post.
#   * nav-js-snippet, site-header-snippet — coupled to shared.css (the snippet's
#     1150px breakpoint matches it), which has a separate guarded publish rail.
#     Publish the coupled assets manually in one sitting until they share one
#     atomic release mechanism.
# Only the *-prod rows of those two pages are here.
# guide-thank-you (4585) is published (returns 200 since September 22, 2026) and ships
# with guide-download (4202) in the same run: 4202 gains the form-side trackLead and
# 4585 drops its on-load generate_lead together, so a guide lead never counts twice.
# The publish script's post_status guard never changes 4585's status. The theme's
# assets/php/functions.php (rtTrack) is still a hand deploy. See
# docs/guide-release-runbook.md, "Counting the funnel".
